shortDescription: Enhances mob equipment and effects for a more engaging gameplay experience.
oneLiner: Hostile mobs spawn kitted out - battle-worn armour, permanent potion effects and, for skeletons, a random enchanted weapon - with the loot table getting nastier below Y=0 and nastiest of all in the Nether and the End.

configKeys.effect: Chance (in percentage) for mobs to drop their enhanced gear upon death (0-100). Written per filled equipment slot via Mob#setDropChance(slot, value/100f); slots the module does not fill keep their vanilla drop chance.

Config comment: "Maximum durability for enhanced gear as percentage (1-100%)". Actually the REMAINING durability in percent (100 = pristine, 1 = nearly broken) and it is applied ONLY to the main-hand weapon (BetterMobsModule.java:141-145), never to armor - armor uses the per-zone ARMOR_DURABILITY rolls instead.

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.entity.EntityJoinLevelEvent (BetterMobsModule.java:62-63, GAME bus via NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this) in onInitialize(), line 51) - the module's only event handler; returns immediately unless the entity is a Monster on a ServerLevel (line 67)
notes:
PROVEN FACTS / GOTCHAS FOR THE DOC WRITER (independently re-verified against the working tree; line numbers are current).

0. SCOPE / SHAPE. The whole module is 3 files: modules/better_mobs/BetterMobsModule.java (598 lines), config/BetterMobsConfig.java (764 lines), config/BetterMobsConfigKey.java (16 lines), plus the standalone entrypoint standalone/better_mobs/BetterMobsStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_better_mobs")). No DeferredRegister anywhere -> no blocks, items, entities, recipes, keybinds. No mixins (nothing named better_mobs in mixin/ or in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json). No commands. No lang keys at all: grep -i "better_mobs|better mobs" over assets/vanillaplusadditions/lang/*.json returns nothing; the only player-visible string is the hardcoded German/English literal in the debug broadcast (BetterMobsModule.java:320). No shouldInitialize() and no isEnabledByDefault() override -> always initializes, defaults to enabled via Module.isEnabledByDefault() (Module.java:73-75). enabled + debug_logging come from AbstractModuleConfig (AbstractModuleConfig.java:58-66) and are deliberately not listed under configKeys.

1. DOCS STATE. There is NO docs/modules/better_mobs.md. README.md:51-52 is the only prose that exists, and Better Mobs is also absent from the README's "Documentation" link list (README.md:292-308) - so this doc would be a genuinely new page, and the README link block needs a new entry.

2. HOW IT WORKS - one event, no mixins. A single @SubscribeEvent on EntityJoinLevelEvent (BetterMobsModule.java:62-63), registered on NeoForge.EVENT_BUS in onInitialize() (line 51). Gates in order: isModuleEnabled() (64) -> entity instanceof Monster && level instanceof ServerLevel (67) -> mob id in enabled_mobs (73). Zone lookup (BetterMobsConfig.java:697-709): Level.END or Level.NETHER -> nether_end regardless of Y; otherwise Y>=0 -> above_zero, Y<0 -> below_zero. below_zero's OWN config comment ("Configuration for mobs spawned below Y=0 or in the Nether/End", BetterMobsConfig.java:88) is therefore wrong/misleading: the Nether and the End never reach below_zero. Worth calling out in the doc.

3. ORDER OF OPERATIONS inside the handler: gear material -> weapon (WEAPON_RANDOMIZER) -> armor (only for mobs in enabled_mobs_with_armor) -> potion effects -> optional debug broadcast.

4. DEAD DEFAULT #1 - shulker never triggers. Only Monster subclasses pass line 67. Verified myself with javap against the decompiled 1.21.1 classes in .gradle/configuration/neoForm/neoFormJoined1.21.1-20240808.144430/raw.jar: net.minecraft.world.entity.monster.Shulker extends net.minecraft.world.entity.animal.AbstractGolem (which extends PathfinderMob) and only *implements* Enemy - it is NOT a Monster. So "minecraft:shulker" in the default enabled_mobs is a permanent no-op. All 19 other defaults were confirmed Monster subclasses by the same javap run: Zombie/Spider/Blaze/Guardian/Warden extend Monster directly; Husk/Drowned/ZombifiedPiglin extend Zombie; Skeleton/Stray/WitherSkeleton extend AbstractSkeleton -> Monster; CaveSpider -> Spider; ElderGuardian -> Guardian; Witch -> Raider -> PatrollingMonster -> Monster; Pillager/Vindicator -> AbstractIllager -> Raider; Evoker/Illusioner -> SpellcasterIllager -> AbstractIllager; Piglin -> AbstractPiglin -> Monster.

5. BY DEFAULT MOST LISTED MOBS ONLY GET POTION EFFECTS. Armor is gated on enabled_mobs_with_armor (BetterMobsModule.java:171), which defaults to just zombie / skeleton / husk / wither_skeleton. Weapons are gated on WEAPON_RANDOMIZER entries, which in all three zones list only minecraft:skeleton. So of the 20 default enabled_mobs: skeleton gets armor + weapon, zombie/husk/wither_skeleton get armor only, shulker gets nothing (see #4), and the remaining 15 (stray, drowned, spider, cave_spider, witch, pillager, vindicator, evoker, illusioner, blaze, guardian, elder_guardian, warden, piglin, zombified_piglin) can only ever receive potion effects. README.md:52 says "mobs can spawn with customizable armor and potion effects" and never mentions weapons at all - the doc should fix that gap and state the skeleton-only default explicitly.

6. TOTAL WEAPON CHANCE for a skeleton (module lines 112-127): randVal = nextInt(100), cumulative over the entries whose parts[0] equals the mob id. Defaults -> 60% above Y=0 (sword 35 + axe 25), 70% below Y=0 (40+30), 80% in Nether/End (45+35). Note the cumulative scheme means the FIRST matching entry effectively wins its share: sword occupies [0,35), axe [35,60), the rest is no weapon.

7. GEAR-TYPE ROLL CAN PRODUCE NOTHING, and then the mob gets NOTHING. Selection walks GEAR_TYPES in list order and takes the first entry whose own independent percentage roll succeeds (BetterMobsConfig.java:545-553, note the break). These are independent rolls, not a weighted table: above Y=0 the defaults gold 10 / chainmail 10 / leather 20 give P(no gear type) = 0.9*0.9*0.8 = 64.8%. below Y=0: 0.9*0.7*0.9*0.7 = 39.7%. nether_end offers only netherite;30 -> 70%. When nothing is picked, GEAR_TYPES comes back as an EMPTY list (never null - BetterMobsConfig.java:683-685 pre-fills every key with List.of()) and the module returns early at BetterMobsModule.java:93-98, BEFORE the weapon block - so such a mob gets neither armor NOR a weapon NOR potion effects. That early-out is the single biggest thing an admin needs to understand: the GEAR_TYPES percentages are the master switch for the whole module, not just for the armor material.

8. WEAPON_TYPES behaves DIFFERENTLY from GEAR_TYPES: it is a proper weighted pick via selectWeightedProperty (BetterMobsConfig.java:711-743) over the sum of the weights, so as long as the list is non-empty and the total weight > 0 it ALWAYS returns a material. The defaults happen to sum to 100 in every zone, which hides the difference - but if an admin edits them to sum to 50 the weights are still normalised, i.e. they behave as relative shares, not as percentages.

9. MATERIAL SPLIT. sword and axe use the WEAPON_TYPES material, everything else (armor, and bow/crossbow/trident which ignore material) uses the GEAR_TYPES material (isMaterialBasedWeapon, BetterMobsModule.java:346-348). In getItemForTypeAndMaterial (lines 430-491) the recognised armor materials are gold/iron/chainmail/leather/diamond/netherite; for sword/axe they are gold/iron/wood/wooden/chainmail/leather/stone/diamond/netherite, where "chainmail" and "leather" both map to the WOODEN sword/axe (lines 471, 480). An unmapped material yields ItemStack.EMPTY; for the weapon the code retries once with the gear material (lines 134-137), for armor it just silently skips the piece. Recognised item types: helmet, chestplate, leggings, boots, sword, axe, bow, crossbow, trident.

10. ARMOR pieces are rolled per slot from ARMOR_CHANCES (BetterMobsConfig.java:536-542) and an armor piece's enchantments are only rolled at all if that piece actually spawned (BetterMobsConfig.java:570-589). WEAPON_ENCHANTMENTS, by contrast, are rolled unconditionally (lines 651-663), so a mob that gets no weapon still burns those rolls - which shifts the shared Random stream but has no visible effect.

11. max_durability APPLIES ONLY TO THE WEAPON, and it is really "remaining durability in percent". Read at BetterMobsModule.java:141 inside the weapon branch and nowhere else; line 144 does setDamageValue(max - max*percent/100), i.e. 100 = pristine, 1 = almost broken. With the shipped default of 100 the weapon spawns undamaged. Armor durability comes from the per-zone ARMOR_DURABILITY min_percent/max_percent instead: four independent rolls, one per slot (BetterMobsConfig.java:631-635, always present), consumed by armorDurabilityPercent (BetterMobsModule.java:500-510) and applied by applyArmorDurability (lines 519-528), which clamps to 1..100 and guarantees the piece is never handed out already broken. The README (line 52) already scopes "battle-worn" correctly to the ARMOR only, so there is no README contradiction here - but the config comment "Maximum durability for enhanced gear as percentage (1-100%)" (BetterMobsConfig.java:76) IS misleading twice over: it is not a maximum, and it does not cover "gear" in general, only the main-hand weapon.

12. ENCHANTMENTS. Two candidate levels are rolled once per mob from ENCHANTMENT_LEVELS min_level/max_level (BetterMobsConfig.java:592-609); applyArmorEnchantments then picks one of the two at random per enchantment (BetterMobsModule.java:541) and clamps it per enchantment via MobArmorEnchantments.clampLevel (line 592) - that clamp is exactly the "no more Unbreaking IV" fix the README advertises, and better_mobs is the only caller of clampLevel in the repo. Exactly 37 vanilla enchantment names are recognised by the hardcoded switch (lines 542-581); any other name is silently dropped. Enchanting is additionally gated on Enchantment#canEnchant and EnchantmentHelper.isEnchantmentCompatible (lines 588-589), so e.g. the default WEAPON_ENCHANTMENTS power/punch/flame entries are simply skipped on a sword or axe, with no warning. applyArmorEnchantments is used for the weapon too, despite its name.

13. DEAD DEFAULT #2 - "haste" does nothing. POTION_EFFECTS;haste is in all three default zone lists (above_zero 5%, below_zero 10%, nether_end 10%), but the effect switch (BetterMobsModule.java:275-300) has no "haste" case and falls into "case null, default -> {}". The 13 recognised names are exactly: speed, strength, regeneration, fire_resistance, invisibility, water_breathing, night_vision, jump_boost, weakness, slowness, mining_fatigue, poison, wither. (So regeneration, invisibility, water_breathing, night_vision, jump_boost, weakness, slowness, mining_fatigue, poison and wither are available but not used by any default.)

14. DEAD RANDOMNESS - effects are always level I and effectively permanent. BetterMobsModule.java:272 rolls new Random(...).nextInt(1, 2); the upper bound is exclusive, so it always returns 1 and the amplifier is always level-1 = 0. Duration is Integer.MAX_VALUE ticks (line 273) - roughly 3.4 years of game time, i.e. the mob keeps its particle trail for good. The debug line nevertheless prints "(Level 1)" as if it were variable.

15. DETERMINISM + RE-APPLICATION. Every roll is seeded from uuid.getLeastSignificantBits() (BetterMobsConfig.java:516, BetterMobsModule.java:99, 272, 539; the weapon roll uses ... ^ 0x5EED at line 112), so a given mob always produces exactly the same gear - two mobs with the same low UUID bits get identical kit, and there is no per-spawn variation. EntityJoinLevelEvent also fires when an existing mob is re-added to the level on chunk reload, so the whole block runs again and re-applies an identical set, which also resets whatever damage the gear had taken and re-writes the drop chances. (The re-fire on chunk reload is a NeoForge/vanilla property and is NOT provable from this repo; the determinism is.)

16. DROP CHANCE is written per equipped slot with setDropChance(slot, drop_chance/100f) - main hand at BetterMobsModule.java:146, head 149, chest 205, legs 227, feet 249. It is applied only to slots the module actually fills.

17. DEBUG MODE IS PLAYER-VISIBLE, NOT JUST A LOG LINE. With debug logging active for this module (debug_logging = ON, or AUTO plus globalDebugLogging = true - AbstractModuleConfig.java:169-186), EVERY equipped spawn broadcasts a chat message to ALL players on the server, with a hover tooltip listing the full gear and a click-to-run "/tp @s <x> <y> <z>" (BetterMobsModule.java:305-338). On a populated server that is a flood, and it is far louder than the generic description in docs/guides/debug-logging.md (which uses better_mobs as its "noisy module" example at line 56 without saying why). The doc should carry an explicit warning. Caveat: the click event runs /tp as the CLICKING player, so it only works for someone with the vanilla permission level for /tp - that part is vanilla behaviour, not provable from this repo.

18. SKELETON AI REFRESH. refreshWeaponBehavior (BetterMobsModule.java:350-360) only calls reassessWeaponGoal() on AbstractSkeleton. If an admin adds a WEAPON_RANDOMIZER entry giving a bow or crossbow to a non-skeleton, that mob keeps its melee AI and will hold the bow without using it.

19. FRAGILE CONFIG PARSING - a malformed zone entry can escape the event handler. splitConfigEntry (BetterMobsConfig.java:753-760) deliberately throws IllegalArgumentException when an entry contains ':' but no ';' (i.e. someone used the old ':' delimiter). In getRandomEquipmentSetupForMob that call sits at line 522, OUTSIDE the try that starts at line 527, and the Integer.parseInt calls on the chance/value fields are unguarded there as well (lines 540, 548, 580, 598, 600, 642, 656, plus 721/735 in selectWeightedProperty and 750 in parseWeaponRandomizer). Nothing on the call path catches it (BetterMobsModule.java:83 calls it bare), so a single malformed entry throws out of onEntityJoinLevel on every mob spawn. Only getDimensionConfigEntries has a try/catch (lines 698-708), and that only covers "config not loaded yet". The convertToKeyMap path (line 443) has the same structure - splitConfigEntry outside the try at 449 - but is dead code (see #21). The doc needs a warning box: entries use ';' as the separator, and every chance field must be an integer.

20. DEAD BRANCH: getRandomEquipmentSetupForMob never returns null (it always returns the map built at BetterMobsConfig.java:517 and pre-filled at 683-685), so the "if (setup == null)" guard plus its debug line at BetterMobsModule.java:84-89 can never execute.

21. DEAD CODE (verified: zero callers anywhere under src/, only self-references inside BetterMobsConfig.java): getAboveZeroConfig() (405), getBelowZeroConfig() (417), getNetherEndConfig() (429), convertToKeyMap() (439, reachable only through those three), isEntityEnabled() (501) and canEntityWearArmor() (508). The module reads getEnabledMobs()/getEnabledMobsWithArmor() directly instead (BetterMobsModule.java:73, 171).

22. CONFIG COMMENT vs DEFAULT MISMATCH: the enabled_mobs comment (BetterMobsConfig.java:98-104) lists the mobs only up to minecraft:warden and omits minecraft:piglin and minecraft:zombified_piglin, which ARE in the actual 20-entry default list (lines 26-47). Cosmetic, but it is what an admin reads in the generated .toml.

23. docs/guides/configuration.md:65-67 uses "WEAPON_RANDOMIZER;minecraft:skeleton;sword;12" as a FORMAT example - that is not a claim about the shipped default (35/40/45 per zone), so it is not an error, but the same paragraph promises "The exact format is documented on each module's own page", and that page does not exist yet (see #1). Documenting the entry grammar is therefore the main job of the new page.

24. SHARED HELPER / PACKAGING. The only cross-module coupling is util/MobArmorEnchantments.clampLevel. build.gradle packs basePkg/util/** into the vpa_core jar (line 615), and renderModuleToml gives every standalone module jar a required dependency on vpa_core (line 510), so the standalone vpa_better_mobs jar resolves it - no moduleDeps entry is needed and none is declared (build.gradle:396). The module jar packs modules/better_mobs/** plus standalone/better_mobs/**; no dataGlobs, no mixins (build.gradle:626-659).

25. TESTING: the repo has no src/test, so there is no automated coverage; verification is in-game only.

26. No TODO/FIXME in BetterMobsModule.java. One TODO in the config: BetterMobsConfig.java:287 - "Unterschiedliche Konfiguration fuer Nether/End, falls gewuenscht bzw. fuer andere Dimensionen". Separate Nether vs. End blocks, and per-dimension configs for modded dimensions, were never implemented: every modded dimension falls into the above_zero/below_zero split by Y.
